text:
sahil: Quick q — how do we want to enforce endpoint-specific limits for chat vs embeddings vs rerank vs streaming? per-key buckets, per-org, or a hybrid?

martin: I vote per-key primary with an endpoint dimension. i.e. bucket keyed by (api_key, endpoint_type). keeps accounting simple and prevents embeddings spikes from killing chat.

tara: streaming is weird — long-lived sockets. do we meter on request start or tokens emitted?

joey: tokens emitted. streaming should be token-bucket measured on send. also add a concurrent-streams cap (leaky-bucket) to protect memory/GPU.

nina: embeddings are extremely bursty (many small requests). allow short bursts (higher capacity in 1s window) but with a cooldown/refill tuned to average rate.

ops-bot: @channel detected spike: org 0123 consuming embeddings 8x baseline in last 2m :warning:

sahil: console UX: need per-route breakdown and a visible "quota inheritance" setting (org cap vs key override). also show estimated p95 latency impact if throttled so product folks can reason.

martin: impl note: use consistent-hash routing to limiter shards, store counters in Redis with INCR+TTL for durability. make the key include endpoint tag (chat|embed|rerank|stream).

dana: can we avoid Redis for streaming hot paths? maybe local in-memory counters with async flush to Redis; if node dies we accept some leniency.

joey: fallback behavior on quota breach: prefer graceful degradation. examples:
- chat: route to smaller model variant or reduce max_tokens
- embeddings: enqueue with backpressure or return 429 with retry semantics
- rerank: apply lightweight heuristic fallback (approximate scoring)
- streaming: cut token rate / close connection with clear Retry-After header

tara: rerank is low-token-high-qps. we need a per-second RPS limiter in front, not just token-buckets.

nina: telemetry requirements: emit per-endpoint metrics: tokens_consumed, requests_rejected, concurrent_streams, avg_burst_size, borrow_from_org_pool_count. tag metrics with rollout_label (canary|global) so we can A/B.

martin: also log limiter decisions with brief reason codes: endpoint_quota, org_pool_exhausted, per_key_rate, rps_limit. small structured field in access logs is enough.

joey: rejecting responses should be helpful. suggestion header/body:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 5
X-RateLimit-Reason: endpoint_quota
```
body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","suggested_action":"try smaller model or reduce batch size","suggested_model":"gpt-medium"}

sahil: policy for shared org-level burst pool? keep a separate borrowable bucket for enterprise customers. it should be gated (exponential backoff) and visible in console usage graphs.

tara: security/abuse note: if org_pool is abused we need automatic throttling + alerting and easy disable in console.

nina: rollout plan idea: enable per-key+endpoint in staging for 7 days, collect telemetry. canary 5% of prod traffic for 48h. metrics to watch: 429 rate, failed requests by customer, latency p95, false-positive fallbacks.

martin: console wiring: add toggle "Auto-fallback to compatible model on quota breach" with short tooltip explaining pros/cons. show expected cost delta.

joey: small chunk of work for API surface: new headers + error codes, plus an event when fallback was triggered (so we can surface in console session trace).

sahil: ok i'll draft the ticket with tasks: schema change (bucket key includes endpoint), limiter service changes + streaming path, telemetry + dashboards, console UI changes, canary runbook, and an incident playbook for misconfig. assigning owners in the ticket.

dana: thanks — please add a short explainer in the ticket for why we chose token-metering for streaming (memory/cost protection).

sahil: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

joey: leaving a tiny nit: ensure rerank requests with <10 tokens are super-cheap and de-prioritized last in org-borrow queue.

tara: noted. adding to ticket.

ops-bot: /note sahil created ticket #INF-4821: per-key+endpoint quotas + streaming token-metering + console UX

sahil: great — next steps: draft design doc and link PRs. end thread.
